lines.trans: Look at Hao's cutting board, Mei—every single carrot cube is identical!
Cubes of the same size cook at the exact same speed, brother. Basic physics!
Laugh all you want, Peng—that is the neatest soup prep my kitchen has ever seen!

words.gloss: all you want; feel free to

lines.trans: The olive oil in the pot is warm—do the onions and carrots go in now?
Yes! Stir three minutes to bring out the sweetness, then add red lentils and hot broth.
Do we add the courtyard thyme and parsley next, chef?
Tie two fresh herb sprigs with string, and add one tiny pinch of salt at the end.
Listening to hot soup simmer gently in a stone kitchen beats city traffic any day!
Funny—three years ago we argued on the phone, and today we make soup together.
Remind me never to wait three years before calling you again, brother.
All right, brothers, save the tears—my bread timer is ringing!
Oven mitts on! Eight crusty loaves coming out of the oven piping hot!

examples.text: 外面一模一样，可是你看里面！

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān. Cardinal number 3; combines with measure words (三个) and floors (三楼).

meanings.note: Pinyin: yě. Always stands directly before the verb or adjective, never at the end of a clause.

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jīn tiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 今天一天 ('all day today').

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǐ hòu. Measure word (量词): 段, e.g. 以后的时间 ('time afterward').

meanings.note: Pinyin: què. Always sits AFTER the subject and BEFORE the verb to mark contrast ('yet, surprisingly').

meanings.note: Pinyin: ma. Placed at the end of any statement to turn it into a neutral yes/no question.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ba. At the end of a sentence, softens commands into friendly suggestions ('let's…') or asks for confirmation.

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。

examples.text: 同事之间有分歧也别吵架。

meanings.note: Pinyin: hé. Joins nouns or pronouns ('A and B'), NEVER two whole clauses; also means 'with' (和你一样).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎng. Used for bells, phones, pipes, or alarms ringing or clanking.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dǔ chē. Separable verb-object compound ('traffic is backed up').

meanings.note: Pinyin: duō. Means 'many' as an adjective, 'how…?' before adjectives (多大), or 'more than' after round numbers (三十多).

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà xiǎo. Antonymic abstract noun combining 大 ('big') + 小 ('small') to mean 'relative size'.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎo. Main adjective 'good'; as a result complement after a verb, means 'ready/completed properly' (修好, 准备好).

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？

examples.text: 今晚这里有最强的明星阵容。
examples.trans: Tonight features the strongest celebrity lineup.

examples.text: 他们团队的执行力非常强。
examples.trans: Their team's execution is very strong.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Read de after a verb to introduce how it goes (走得快 'walk fast'); read děi before a verb to mean 'must'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. As an adjective/adverb, 'fast/quickly'; in 快…了, 'about to'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 小晴，快看里面！这不是我的箱子！
examples.trans: Qing, look inside quickly! This is not my case!

meanings.note: Pinyin: màn màn. Polite host phrase: 慢慢吃 ('take your time eating'), 慢慢走 ('walk safely').

examples.text: 凉？啊——对！老街水管早上需要慢慢热身！
examples.trans: Cool? Ah—yes! Old-street water pipes need a gentle morning warm-up!

examples.text: 把蓝色转轮慢慢往左拧开——别太快。
examples.trans: Turn the blue wheel open slowly to the left—not too fast.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ men. First-person plural pronoun; add 的 for 'our' (我们的).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: dài. Specifically for accessories placed on the head, face, neck, or wrist—contrast 穿 for clothes/shoes.

examples.text: 哎呀，怎么拿错了！我戴眼镜看看行李牌。
examples.trans: Dear me, what a mix-up! Let me put on my glasses and check the luggage tag.

examples.text: 完了！昨天我没戴眼镜，在平板上接了电话预订！
examples.trans: Disaster! Yesterday without my glasses I took a phone booking on the tablet!

meanings.note: Pinyin: biǎn dòu. Literally 扁 ('flat') + 豆 ('bean/legume'), used for flat-podded beans and lentils.

examples.text: 加了柠檬和橄榄油的金黄扁豆汤又香又暖胃。
examples.trans: Golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil is fragrant and warming.

examples.text: 小美前一天晚上先把扁豆洗干净泡好。
examples.trans: Mei washed and soaked the lentils the night before.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shǒu tào. Combines 手 ('hand') + 套 ('protective sheath/cover'); measure word: 双 (shuāng, pair) or 只 (zhī, single); verb: 戴 (dài).

examples.text: 快戴上厚厚的烤箱手套，八个脆皮面包热腾腾出炉啦！
examples.trans: Quickly put on thick oven mitts—eight loaves of crusty bread are coming piping hot out of the oven!

examples.text: 冬天在院子里修剪树枝的时候，老陈总会戴上一双帆布手套。
examples.trans: When pruning branches in the courtyard in winter, Chen always puts on a pair of canvas gloves.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cái. Signals that something happened later than expected or in a small amount—contrast 就.

examples.text: 老砖房顶楼平时要等很久水才热。
examples.trans: Top floors in old brick houses usually wait ages before the water warms up.

examples.text: 因为房子只是砖头和木头，志鹏，家人才是留住的东西。
examples.trans: Because a house is only brick and timber, Zhipeng—family is what we keep.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dǎ diàn huà. Separable verb-object phrase: 打 ('make/dial') + 电话 ('telephone'); recipient takes 给 (给老陈打电话).

examples.text: 周经理早上打电话订了花园木椅。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou made a phone call in the morning to order wooden garden chairs.

examples.text: 到车站以后记得给我打个电话。
examples.trans: Remember to give me a phone call once you reach the station.

meanings.note: Pinyin: diào. As a verb, 'drop'; after another verb, marks removal or disposal (关掉 'turn off', 擦掉 'wipe away').

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

examples.text: 冬天用掉最后一个了。只有桥那边的老五金店有这个尺寸。
examples.trans: Used the last one in winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge carries this size.

meanings.en: next; after this; in the next step
meanings.note: Pronounced jiē xiàlái; used sentence-initially as a discourse connector (especially by hosts and directors) or before 的 + noun ('the upcoming...').

examples.text: 接下来抓紧时间，把最终稿交上来。
examples.trans: Next, make good use of the time and hand in the final draft.

examples.text: 女士们，先生们，接下来有请今晚的神秘嘉宾！
examples.trans: Ladies and gentlemen, up next please welcome tonight's mystery guest!

meanings.note: Verb tíxǐng ('remind, tip off').

examples.text: 快提醒他上个月跳槽的那个女主持人。
examples.trans: Remind him of the female host who left last month.

examples.text: 谢谢你提醒我带雨伞。
examples.trans: Thank you for reminding me to bring an umbrella.

撮.gloss: pinch (measure word for salt, tea leaves, or powder)

meanings.en: pinch (measure word for salt, tea leaves, or powder)
meanings.note: Pinyin: cuō. Classifier for a tiny quantity picked up between thumb and fingertips (一小撮盐 'a small pinch of salt').

examples.text: 用细绳绑两小枝新鲜香草，最后再往汤里放一小撮盐。
examples.trans: Tie two small sprigs of fresh herbs with string, and finally add a small pinch of salt to the soup.

examples.text: 泡茶的时候抓一小撮干薄荷叶放进壶里，香气马上就出来了。
examples.trans: Toss a small pinch of dried mint leaves into the pot when brewing tea and the aroma rises at once.

meanings.note: Pinyin: fàng. Everyday verb for placing an object somewhere (放在桌子上).

examples.text: 我们不知道。有人放在台阶上，按了门铃。
examples.trans: We do not know. Someone set it on the step and rang the bell.

examples.text: 小勺子和餐巾放在哪里？
examples.trans: Where do the small spoons and napkins go?

related.gloss: handle with care (lift gently, set down gently)

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhěng qí. Describes neatly arranged keys, chairs, or handwriting.

examples.text: 上面怎么用铅笔整齐画了这条街三家客栈？
examples.trans: Why are three inns on this street neatly sketched in pencil on it?

examples.text: 明信片上整齐的方格字，我两秒钟就认出来了。
examples.trans: That neat block handwriting on the postcard—I recognized it in two seconds.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīn xiān. Describes fresh fruit, fresh juice, or fresh herbs.

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 闻闻看！热面包、热炒蛋，还有新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot scrambled eggs, and fresh herbs.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuì. Superlative adverb placed before adjectives or feeling verbs (最好 'best', 最喜欢 'like best').

examples.text: 只有裙子、乐谱，还有我最喜欢的茶杯！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 最上面架子上金色包装那包。怎么了？
examples.trans: The gold-wrapped packet on the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuì hòu. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 最后一个 ('the last one').

examples.text: 上楼梯，平台往左拐，最上面最后一扇门。
examples.trans: Up the stairs, turn left at the landing, last door at the very top.

examples.text: 冬天用掉最后一个了。只有桥那边的老五金店有这个尺寸。
examples.trans: Used the last one in winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge carries this size.

meanings.note: Adjective yǒuyìsi ('interesting, fun').

examples.text: 我今天想跟你聊一件更有意思的事。
examples.trans: Today I want to chat about something far more interesting.

examples.text: 这个访谈选题既有深度又很有意思。
examples.trans: This interview topic has both depth and real charm.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhī. Classifier for slender plant stems, flower sprays, or herb sprigs (两小枝香草 'two small sprigs of herbs', 一枝玫瑰 'a rose stem').

examples.text: 小美让志鹏用细棉绳绑好两小枝刚摘下来的新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Mei had Peng tie two small sprigs of freshly picked herbs together with fine cotton string.

examples.text: 小晴在玻璃花瓶里插了一枝嫩绿的枝叶，桌子一下子亮了起来。
examples.trans: Qing placed a sprig of fresh green foliage in the glass vase, brightening the table right up.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gǎn lǎn yóu. Combines 橄榄 ('olive') + 油 ('oil').

examples.text: 在热扁豆汤里滴几滴橄榄油，味道更香醇。
examples.trans: Adding a few drops of olive oil to hot lentil soup makes it even richer.

examples.text: 小美用橄榄油和新鲜香草烤了一盘番茄。
examples.trans: Mei roasted a tray of tomatoes with olive oil and fresh herbs.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ōu qín. Combines 欧 ('European') + 芹 ('celery/parsley family herb'): flat-leaf or curly garden parsley.

examples.text: 主厨，接下来要往扁豆汤里放院子种的百里香和欧芹吗？
examples.trans: Chef, should we add the thyme and parsley from the courtyard to the lentil soup next?

examples.text: 出锅以前撒一点切碎的新鲜欧芹，热汤看起来翠绿诱人。
examples.trans: Sprinkle a little chopped fresh parsley right before serving and the hot soup looks bright green and inviting.

meanings.note: Pinyin: měi. Usually followed by a measure word (每个星期 'every week', 每位客人 'every guest').

examples.text: 每个蓝杯子旁边放一张餐巾和一把小勺子。
examples.trans: Beside every blue cup, put one napkin and one small spoon.

examples.text: 老房子每到星期二就松一颗螺丝。坐吧。
examples.trans: Every Tuesday an old house loosens one screw. Sit down.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bǐ. Forms comparisons in A 比 B + adj ('A is more adj than B').

examples.text: 说实话，我比以前灰色办公室喜欢这儿多了。
examples.trans: Honestly, I like this place far better than my old grey office.

examples.text: 听听他说的！老陈比我们好奇两倍！
examples.trans: Listen to him! Chen is twice as curious as we are!

meanings.note: Pinyin: tāng. Measure word (量词): 碗 (wǎn), e.g. 一碗汤 ('a bowl of soup').

examples.text: 先生，给您干毛巾擦外套，还有一碗热汤。
examples.trans: Sir, here is a dry towel to wipe your coat, plus a bowl of hot soup.

examples.text: 热汤？在冷雨中走过来之后，这听起来太棒了。
examples.trans: Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.

related.gloss: a bowl of soup (measure word 碗)

meanings.note: Pinyin: yáng cōng. Combines 洋 ('foreign/introduced from overseas') + 葱 ('allium/scallion'); measure word: 个 (gè) or 颗 (kē).

examples.text: 锅里的橄榄油热了，洋葱和胡萝卜现在可以下锅了吗？
examples.trans: The olive oil in the pot is warm—should the onions and carrots go into the pot now?

examples.text: 把洋葱用小火慢慢炒三分钟，就能炒出自然的甜味。
examples.trans: Sauté the onions gently over low heat for three minutes to bring out their natural sweetness.

meanings.note: Media verb chǎo ('manufacture buzz; stir-fry').

examples.text: 想要借着星天的平台炒炒热度，没问题。
examples.trans: Wanting to stir up a bit of buzz on Xingtian's platform is fine.

examples.text: 这盘家常菜刚炒出来，趁热吃吧。
examples.trans: This home-style dish was just stir-fried—eat it hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kǎo xiāng. Measure word (量词): 台, e.g. 一台烤箱 ('an oven').

examples.text: 还好烤箱里的面团已经放进去了。
examples.trans: My dough is already in the oven, at least.

examples.text: 宋老师早！我的肉桂卷刚出烤箱。
examples.trans: Morning, Teacher Song! My cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè. Describes hot tea, hot water, or warm weather.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 厨房里炖着一锅鲜美的热汤，满屋子都是香味。
examples.trans: A pot of savory hot soup is simmering in the kitchen, filling the whole house with its aroma.

examples.text: 请趁热喝下这碗热汤，身上的寒气马上就散了。
examples.trans: Please drink this bowl of hot soup while it is hot, and the chill in your bones will vanish right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè téng téng. Vivid ABB adjective 热 ('hot') + 腾腾 ('rising in puffs of steam'), used for bread fresh from the oven or bowls of hot soup.

examples.text: 八个金黄的脆皮面包热腾腾出炉啦，快戴上烤箱手套！
examples.trans: Eight golden loaves of crusty bread are coming piping hot out of the oven—put on your oven mitts!

examples.text: 志豪端出一大锅热腾腾的红扁豆汤，香气一下子充满了厨房。
examples.trans: Hao brought out a big pot of steaming hot red lentil soup, filling the kitchen with fragrance.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǔ. Core culinary verb for cooking in liquid (煮汤 'simmer soup', 煮茶 'brew tea by boiling', 煮面 'boil noodles').

examples.text: 真有意思，三年前我们在电话里吵架，今天却一起在厨房煮汤。
examples.trans: Funny how three years ago we argued on the phone, and today we are cooking soup together in the kitchen.

examples.text: 厨房炉子上的红扁豆汤已经用小火慢慢煮了四十分钟。
examples.trans: The red lentil soup on the kitchen stove has been simmering gently over low heat for forty minutes.

meanings.note: Adjective shú ('well acquainted with').

examples.text: 您上周还说我熟那边。
examples.trans: Last week you said I knew that area well.

examples.text: 我跟这儿的同事都很熟。
examples.trans: I know the colleagues here very well.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wù lǐ. Combines 物 ('matter/things') + 理 ('underlying principle/law of nature').

examples.text: 志豪一本正经地说：“大小一样的菜丁熟得一样快，这是基本物理！”
examples.trans: Hao said earnestly, 'Vegetable cubes of the same size cook at the same speed—that is basic physics!'

examples.text: 无论是修钢琴的琴弦还是烤面包，背后其实都有有趣的物理道理。
examples.trans: Whether tuning piano strings or baking bread, there are fascinating principles of physics behind both.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàn zài. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 现在这时候 ('this moment right now').

examples.text: 现在他的箱子还安全锁着呢。
examples.trans: For now, his suitcase stays safely locked up.

examples.text: 太好了！现在我想吃一顿丰盛的早餐。
examples.trans: Wonderful! Now I would like to eat a big breakfast.

related.gloss: this moment right now (measure word 个)

meanings.note: Pinyin: tián wèi. Combines 甜 ('sweet') + 味 ('taste/flavour').

examples.text: 把洋葱丁和胡萝卜丁先炒三分钟，就能炒出自然的甜味。
examples.trans: Sautéing the diced onions and carrots for three minutes first brings out their natural sweetness.

examples.text: 柠檬汁的酸香配上蜂蜜的甜味，喝起来恰到好处。
examples.trans: The bright tang of lemon juice paired with the sweetness of honey tastes just right.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòng. Works as main verb ('use a key') or preposition ('with/using').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

meanings.note: Pinyin: diàn huà. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个电话 ('a phone call').

examples.text: 上面有名字或者电话号码吗？
examples.trans: Is there a name or a phone number on it?

examples.text: 可惜没有电话号码，只有两个字母和老街名字。
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number, only two letters and an old street name.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎi lǐ xiāng. Literally 百里 ('a hundred li') + 香 ('fragrant'): aromatic culinary herb thyme (*Thymus vulgaris*).

examples.text: 志鹏去院子的花坛边摘了两小枝新鲜的百里香和欧芹。
examples.trans: Peng went to the courtyard flowerbed and picked two small sprigs of fresh thyme and parsley.

examples.text: 炖蔬菜高汤的时候放一枝百里香，整锅汤都会带着温和的草木清香。
examples.trans: Add a sprig of thyme when simmering vegetable stock and the whole pot takes on a gentle herbal aroma.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: yán. Core culinary noun for table or sea salt; measure word: 勺 (sháo, spoonful) or 撮 (cuō, pinch).

examples.text: 用细绳绑好新鲜香草放进锅里，最后再加一小撮盐调味。
examples.trans: Tie the fresh herbs with string and put them in the pot, then add a small pinch of salt at the end.

examples.text: 小晴给右边的白瓷罐贴上了“盐”字标签，免得大家再跟白糖弄混。
examples.trans: Qing stuck a 'Salt' label on the white ceramic jar on the right so nobody would confuse it with sugar again.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kàn. Covers looking at something, reading silently, or visiting someone; add 见/到 for 'catch sight of'.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhēn. Exclamatory adverb before adjectives (真好！ 'How nice!') or adjective 'genuine'.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

examples.text: 真奇怪！我们坐同一班早火车到同一个区。
examples.trans: How strange! We rode the very same morning train to the same district.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǎn lèi. Combines 眼 ('eye') + 泪 ('tears'); common verb collocations: 掉眼泪 ('shed tears'), 流眼泪 ('cry'), 擦眼泪 ('wipe tears').

examples.text: 小美笑着打趣道：“好啦，两兄弟，先别掉眼泪——我的面包计时器响了！”
examples.trans: Mei teased warmly, 'All right, brothers, no shedding tears yet—my bread timer just went off!'

examples.text: 切洋葱的时候如果怕熏出眼泪，可以先把洋葱放在冷水里泡一下。
examples.trans: If you want to avoid shedding tears when chopping onions, soak the peeled onion briefly in cold water first.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí tou. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块石头 ('a stone').

examples.text: 我来帮您。哎呀，里面装了石头吗？
examples.trans: Let me help you. Goodness, did you pack stones inside?

examples.text: 等等，低头看石头台阶上。
examples.trans: Wait—look down on the stone step.

meanings.note: Verb/noun xiào ('smile, laugh').

examples.text: 你看着我的笔记笑什么？
examples.trans: Why are you smiling at my notes?

examples.text: 听到这个好消息，大家都开心地笑了。
examples.trans: Hearing the good news, everyone smiled happily.

meanings.note: Pinyin: děng. Everyday verb for waiting (等一下 'wait a moment').

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

examples.text: 等一下，小晴……你拿了哪一包黄油？
examples.trans: Wait a second, Qing... which packet of butter did you grab?

meanings.note: Pinyin: hóng. Describes the color red; note that 红茶 is what English calls 'black tea'.

examples.text: 告诉他们，我箱子上面口袋里有红丝带！
examples.trans: Tell them there is a red ribbon inside the top pocket of my case!

examples.text: 我的行李箱！快打开上面口袋……对，红丝带！
examples.trans: My suitcase! Let me open the top pocket... yes, the red ribbon!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xì. Describes slender tools (细镊子 'thin tweezers'), fine grit (细砂纸), or careful work.

examples.text: 明天早上给我一把细镊子和一点木工胶水就行。
examples.trans: Just give me thin tweezers and a little woodworking glue tomorrow morning.

examples.text: 春天的细雨轻轻落在院子的常春藤叶上。
examples.trans: Fine spring rain fell softly onto the ivy leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎng. Action verb for tying herbs, parcels, or cords into a bundle with string or ribbon.

examples.text: 小美教志鹏用细棉绳绑好两小枝新鲜香草，做成香草束放进汤锅。
examples.trans: Mei showed Peng how to tie two small sprigs of fresh herbs with fine cotton string to make a herb bundle for the soup pot.

examples.text: 老陈把修剪下来的树枝整整齐齐绑成一捆，放在院子角落。
examples.trans: Chen tied the pruned branches neatly into a bundle and set them in the corner of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gěi. As main verb, 'give'; as preposition/complement, marks the recipient (给你 'for/to you', 递给我 'pass to me').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shéng. General noun for twisted cord or twine (细绳 'fine string/twine', 棉绳 'cotton string'); measure word: 根 (gēn) or 条 (tiáo).

examples.text: 用一根干净的厨房细绳把百里香和欧芹绑在一起，煮完汤方便捞出来。
examples.trans: Tie the thyme and parsley together with a clean piece of kitchen twine so they are easy to lift out after simmering.

examples.text: 木牌上面系着一根结实的麻绳，正好可以挂在大门口的铁钩上。
examples.trans: A sturdy hemp cord is tied to the top of the wooden sign so it hangs right on the iron hook outside the gate.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hú luó bo. Combines 胡 ('introduced via Central Asia/Silk Road') + 萝卜 ('radish/root vegetable'); final syllable is neutral tone; measure word: 根 (gēn).

examples.text: 志豪菜板上的每一颗胡萝卜丁都切得一模一样。
examples.trans: Every single cube of diced carrot on Hao's chopping board is cut identically.

examples.text: 把胡萝卜和洋葱用橄榄油炒香，煮出来的红扁豆汤颜色金黄。
examples.trans: Sautéing carrots and onions in olive oil gives the simmered red lentil soup a golden glow.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cuì pí. Combines 脆 ('crisp/crunchy') + 皮 ('crust/skin'), especially for artisanal bread (脆皮面包 'crusty bread').

examples.text: 下雨的下午，一碗浓番茄汤配热脆皮面包最舒服了。
examples.trans: On a rainy afternoon, a bowl of rich tomato soup with warm crusty bread is pure comfort.

examples.text: 刚烤好的法式脆皮面包一掰开就咔嚓响。
examples.trans: Freshly baked crusty bread crackles crisp when broken open.

meanings.note: cài — general term for prepared dishes in a meal or leafy vegetables (measure word 道 dào or 盘 pán for dishes)
colloquial slang in 是某人的菜, meaning someone or something that suits one's personal or romantic taste

examples.text: 这个是你的菜吧？不好意思了！
examples.trans: This one is your type, right? Now you are embarrassed!

examples.text: 你觉得他们家菜还合口吧？
examples.trans: Do the dishes at this place suit your taste?

meanings.note: Pinyin: cài bǎn. Combines 菜 ('vegetables/food') + 板 ('wooden board'); synonymous with 砧板; measure word: 块 (kuài).

examples.text: 快看志豪的木头菜板，上面排着整整齐齐的胡萝卜丁和洋葱丁。
examples.trans: Look at Hao's wooden chopping board, lined with neat rows of diced carrots and onions.

examples.text: 切完蔬菜以后，志鹏马上用温水把菜板洗干净立在架子上晾干。
examples.trans: Right after chopping the vegetables, Peng washed the cutting board with warm water and stood it on the rack to dry.

meanings.en: want; need; will / be going to
meanings.note: Pinyin: yào. Direct verb for ordering/requesting ('want'), obligation ('need to'), or imminent future (要下雨了).

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiàn. Appears in farewells (再见, 明天见) and as result complement of perception (看见, 听见).

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

examples.text: 老陈，听得见吗？我刚经过绿药店！
examples.trans: Chen, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jì shí qì. Compound 计时 ('count/measure time') + 器 ('instrument/device'); measure word: 个 (gè).

examples.text: 先别掉眼泪，我的厨房面包计时器叮铃铃响了！
examples.trans: Don't shed tears just yet—my kitchen bread timer just rang!

examples.text: 小美把烤箱旁边的计时器定在三十五分钟，提醒志鹏准时取面包。
examples.trans: Mei set the timer beside the oven for thirty-five minutes to remind Peng to take the bread out on time.

meanings.note: Pinyin: guò. Read neutral-tone guo after a verb for 'have ever done' (见过); read guò as a verb meaning 'cross/pass' (过河 'cross the river').

examples.text: 早跟你说过，那个平板是个坑。
examples.trans: Told you before, that tablet is a trap.

examples.text: 出门左拐，直走到桥。要过河吗？
examples.trans: Left out the gate, straight to the bridge. Do I cross the river?

examples.text: 这是什么套啊？
examples.trans: What kind of setup?

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 里面 ('the inside').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

meanings.note: Pinyin: guō. General culinary vessel for boiling, simmering, or stir-frying; measure word: 口 (kǒu) or 个 (gè).

examples.text: 锅里的橄榄油已经热了，可以把洋葱丁和胡萝卜丁放进去了。
examples.trans: The olive oil in the pot is warm now, so we can put in the diced onions and carrots.

examples.text: 石头厨房的炉灶上炖着一大锅香气四溢的红扁豆汤。
examples.trans: A big pot of fragrant red lentil soup is simmering on the stove in the stone kitchen.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yuàn zi. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个院子 ('a courtyard').

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: miàn bāo. Measure word (量词): 片 (piàn), e.g. 一片面包 ('a slice of bread').

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 闻闻看！热面包、热炒蛋，还有新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot scrambled eggs, and fresh herbs.

related.gloss: a slice of bread (measure word 片)

颗.gloss: measure word for small round things

meanings.en: measure word for small round things
meanings.note: Pinyin: kē. Counts stars, pearls, beans, buttons, and hearts (一颗星 'a star').

examples.text: 老房子每到星期二就松一颗螺丝。坐吧。
examples.trans: Every Tuesday an old house loosens one screw. Sit down.

examples.text: 小盘子里放着五颗新鲜草莓。
examples.trans: Five fresh strawberries sit on the small plate.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiāng cǎo. Measure word (量词): 盆, e.g. 一盆香草 ('a pot of herbs').

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 老陈，这些香草是你自己种的吗？
examples.trans: Chen, did you grow these herbs yourself?

related.gloss: a pot of herbs (measure word 盆)

meanings.note: Pinyin: gāo tāng. Combines 高 ('fine/rich/elevated') + 汤 ('soup/stock'): clear, flavourful culinary stock simmered from vegetables or bones.

examples.text: 把洋葱和胡萝卜炒出甜味以后，再加红扁豆和热高汤。
examples.trans: Once you sauté the onions and carrots until sweet, add the red lentils and hot broth.

examples.text: 小美每天早上都会用新鲜蔬菜和香草熬一锅清澈金黄的高汤。
examples.trans: Every morning Mei simmers a pot of clear golden stock from fresh vegetables and herbs.
